---
title: "06 · The t-test as a linear model"
subtitle: "Week 2"
---

::: {.guiding-q}
Isn't a t-test something else?
:::

## In this session

- The independent-samples *t*-test is a regression with one binary predictor
- The one-sample and the paired *t*-test are intercept-only models
- Welch's *t*-test and what it changes (unequal variances)
- Why this matters: one framework instead of a decision tree of tests

::: {.key-terms}
**Key terms:** [*p*-value](../../glossary.qmd#p-value), [Degrees of freedom](../../glossary.qmd#df)
:::

## Learning goals

After this session you can

- reproduce a *t*-test with `lm()` and show that the results are identical,
- explain what the intercept and the slope correspond to in a *t*-test,
- run a paired *t*-test as a model of differences.

## Simulate first

```{r}
set.seed(6)
group <- factor(rep(c("young", "old"), each = 25), levels = c("young", "old"))
y     <- rnorm(50, ifelse(group == "old", 12, 10), 3)

t.test(y ~ group, var.equal = TRUE)$statistic   # classic t-test
summary(lm(y ~ group))$coefficients             # same t (sign flipped), same p
```

::: {.box}
**Paired *t*-test** = intercept-only model of the differences: `lm(after - before ~ 1)`.
:::
